title: Staining and Imaging of Mouse Submandibular Ganglion by α-Bungarotoxin and Nanosensor
author: Hongrong Yang
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.wxrffm6
materials: Soak submandibular ganglion in 500 µL 0.000002 Molarity (M) α-Bungarotoxin Alexa Fluor 647 conjugated Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #B35450 for 00:30:00 . Alternatively, soak submandibular ganglion in 500 µL nanosensor solution formulated by Clark Lab for 00:30:00

1. Rinse submandibular ganglion with PBS for 00:20:00 2. Soak submandibular ganglion in 500 µL 0.000002 Molarity (M) α-Bungarotoxin Alexa Fluor 647 conjugated Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #B35450 for 00:30:00 . Alternatively, soak submandibular ganglion in 500 µL nanosensor solution formulated by Clark Lab for 00:30:00 3. Rinse submandibular ganglion with PBS for 00:20:00 .

steps.title: Dissect Salivary Ducts and Ganglion
steps.instruction: Isolate the submandibular ganglion by dissecting the salivary ducts from the mouse.

substeps.instruction: Make a midline incision in the neck and expose the salivary glands.
Separate the pair of salivary glands and expose the salivary ducts.
Remove connective tissues surrounding salivary ducts.
Cut the ducts from where they enter salivary glands to where they enter digastric muscles to isolate the submandibular ganglion attached to the ducts.

steps.title: Prepare Ganglion for Imaging
steps.instruction: Mount the submandibular ganglion for confocal microscopy.

substeps.instruction: Place the submandibular ganglion on a glass slide.
Cover the tissue with a cover slip.

steps.title: Image Submandibular Ganglion
steps.instruction: Perform confocal imaging of the whole tissue using a Zeiss LSM 700 (ZEN pro ZEISS software).

substeps.instruction: Use 488 nm laser line for GFP and Oregan Green 488 channel.
Use 555 nm laser line for pHAb.
Use 639 nm laser line for bungarotoxin-Alexa Fluor 647 channel.
Set laser power at 2% or at the appropriate power intensity to clearly see cellular structures.
